steps.text: Diana was in a room with at least two men. Polaroid check — men: Arthur, Elliot, Fenwick, Gregor, Horatio, Jules and Leopold. Fewer than two of them can still reach the Bedroom, so Diana cannot be there.
Ray block: Arthur can only be at the marked tiles, and those tiles all lie on one sightline. Whichever one Arthur takes, the whole stretch is watched, so nobody else can stand on the marked tiles.

Jules was alone in the room, but Fenwick must be in the Music Room, Gregor must be in the Gallery, Isabel must be in the Billiards, Bridget and Elliot must be in the Cellar and Horatio must be in the Foyer, so Jules cannot be in any of them.

Horatio was alone and can only be in the Foyer, so nobody else can be in the Foyer.
Jules was alone and can only be in the Orangery, so nobody else can be in the Orangery.
Fenwick was west of Leopold. Leopold can reach column 6 at most, so Fenwick must be in columns 1–5; Fenwick is in column 5 at the earliest, so Leopold must be in columns 6–11.
Fenwick “was beside a gramophone and was west of Leopold”: of the 3 tiles that fit, only r8c5 is still open. Place Fenwick there.
Leopold “was beside a potted palm”: every tile that fits is ruled out except r7c6. Place Leopold there.
